title: Beyond Fixed Variables: Expanding-variate Time Series Forecasting via Flat Scheme and Spatio-temporal Focal Learning

problem.claim: Existing multivariate time series forecasting generally assumes a fixed number of variables, while real-world cyber-physical systems may add sensors over time.

gap.claim: Expanding-variate forecasting must handle inconsistent data shapes and imbalanced spatio-temporal learning caused by limited observations for newly added variables.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces Expanding-variate Time Series Forecasting as a forecasting task for settings where the number of variables grows over time.
STEV is a flexible spatio-temporal forecasting framework that uses a Flat Scheme to make graph-based modeling variable-scale-agnostic while preserving dynamic spatial correlations.
STEV uses Spatio-temporal Focal Learning with a negative filter and focal contrastive loss to focus optimization on expanding variables.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the EVTSF task, Flat Scheme, and Spatio-temporal Focal Learning strategy as novel introductions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report benchmarking EVTSF on three real-world datasets from various domains against three potential solutions based on state-of-the-art multivariate forecasting models.
The authors report that STEV significantly outperforms its competitors, particularly for expanding variables.
The authors report that STEV using only 5% of observations during the expanding period performs on par with state-of-the-art models trained on complete data.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multivariate time series forecasting commonly assumes a fixed variable count, but deployed sensors can increase that count.
Expanding-variate forecasting introduces inconsistent data shapes and imbalanced learning because new variables have limited observations.
STEV addresses the task with a Flat Scheme and Spatio-temporal Focal Learning.
The framework is evaluated on three real-world datasets against three model-based comparison solutions.
The authors report superior performance, parity with complete-data models at 5% expanding-period observations, and generalizability across expanding scenarios.

source_observation.claim: Flattening samples along the variable dimension is reported to make the model variable-scale-agnostic while preserving dynamic spatial correlations.

interpretation.claim: A representation that avoids fixed-shape assumptions may support forecasting when the set of observed variables changes.

application.claim: Consider variable-dimension-agnostic representations for sensor or feature streams that expand over time.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach transfers beyond the reported expanding-variate forecasting setting.

source_observation.claim: The reported framework focuses optimization on expanding variables using focal contrastive learning and achieves parity with complete-data models using 5% of expanding-period observations.

interpretation.claim: Targeting the least-observed variables may improve performance under uneven observation availability.

application.claim: In evolving monitoring systems, prioritize learning objectives for newly added or data-sparse variables.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the operational conditions, data distributions, or limits under which the 5% result holds.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide dataset names, sizes, splits, or expanding-period definitions.
The abstract does not specify competitor model identities, hyperparameters, metrics, or statistical uncertainty.
The abstract does not describe computational cost, implementation details, or failure cases.
